stories.body: Russian drones struck Kyiv's Pivnichnyi Bridge again on Sunday, damaging a heating main and temporarily disrupting hot water in the northeastern Desnyanskyi district, as Moscow intensified attacks on the capital's infrastructure. The strike came during a surprise visit by German Chancellor Friedrich Merz, who met President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, reaffirmed German support and said Ukraine could expect important new agreements. Reports said Germany was preparing substantial military assistance, including interceptor drones, support for long-range weapons production and funds to repair damaged energy infrastructure. Russia said the bridges were used for military transfers and repeated its warning for foreign nationals to leave Kyiv.
stories.headline: Russian drone strikes hit Kyiv bridges as German Chancellor Merz makes surprise visit

stories.body: Brazilians are voting in the first round of a closely fought presidential election between left-wing incumbent Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, seeking a fourth non-consecutive term, and right-wing Senator Flávio Bolsonaro, son of jailed former president Jair Bolsonaro. Polls have shown the contenders alternating as frontrunners, and a runoff is scheduled for 25 October if neither wins an outright majority. The campaign has highlighted Brazil's deep polarization, with Lula presenting himself as a defender of national independence and Bolsonaro aligning himself with Donald Trump and the regional right.
stories.headline: Brazil votes in closely contested presidential election between Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro

stories.body: Voters in Bosnia and Herzegovina are electing members of the country's tripartite presidency, national parliament and institutions in its two entities in one of the world's most complex electoral systems. The vote takes place amid persistent ethnic divisions rooted in the 1992-95 war, frustration with entrenched political parties and delayed progress toward European Union membership. Separatist rhetoric from Serb nationalist forces remains central to the campaign, while Russia is accused of using close ties with the Serb-led Alliance of Independent Social Democrats to impede Bosnia's European path. New ballot-scanning and biometric verification systems are being used to reduce fraud.
stories.headline: Bosnians vote in election shaped by ethnic tensions and concerns over Russian influence

stories.body: Iran said the Strait of Hormuz will remain closed until the United States fulfills seven conditions that Tehran says were agreed in a memorandum of understanding. A senior Iranian negotiator said the era of delaying talks and imposing demands was over, as reports said US aircraft carriers were heading toward the Middle East to strengthen Central Command's capabilities.
stories.headline: Iran says Strait of Hormuz will remain closed until US meets agreed conditions

stories.body: The Saudi-led coalition dismissed as misleading a Houthi claim that the group had struck an Aramco oil facility near Riyadh with missiles and drones, after reports of flames and smoke south of the Saudi capital. The Houthis also accused Saudi forces of carrying out 26 strikes on Sanaa. The exchange comes amid intensified fighting between the Iran-aligned Houthis and Yemen's internationally recognized government, with government forces claiming hundreds of Houthi fighters were killed in recent operations.
stories.headline: Saudi-led coalition rejects Houthi claim of attack on oil facility near Riyadh

stories.body: Authorities in the United Arab Emirates, Saudi Arabia and Australia are investigating after a Flydubai co-pilot allegedly attacked the captain of a Dubai-to-Tel Aviv flight with a crash axe, sending the aircraft into a steep descent before passengers subdued him. Two reserve pilots aboard the flight then helped land the plane safely in Saudi Arabia. Australian federal police are examining the suspect's links to Australia, where he reportedly studied between 2015 and 2017, while investigators seek to establish his motive and any extremist connections. The injured captain is reported to be in stable condition.
stories.headline: Investigation continues into Flydubai Flight 1073 cockpit attack

stories.body: The US Supreme Court is set to consider a case that could shape whether state and local governments can pursue major oil companies for the costs of climate change. Boulder, Colorado, is pursuing litigation modeled in part on successful cases against tobacco and opioid companies, seeking to establish whether fossil-fuel producers can be held financially responsible for harms linked to their emissions.
stories.headline: Supreme Court case could determine whether major oil companies can be held liable for climate costs

stories.body: Republican officials are pressing Donald Trump's political operation to spend more in Texas as the Senate race between GOP nominee Ken Paxton and Democrat James Talarico tightens. Senate Leadership Fund has committed a record $131 million through a Texas-focused political committee, while Trump-aligned groups are expected to spend roughly $45 million through 12 October. Republicans fear that the escalating cost of defending a traditionally safe state could divert resources from competitive races elsewhere, and some blame Paxton's campaign missteps, including leaked remarks criticizing a Trump convention.
stories.headline: Republicans increase spending to defend Ken Paxton in competitive Texas Senate race

stories.body: Tennessee's prisons chief has resigned following the failed execution of Christa Pike, who remains in critical condition after surviving two lethal injections. Governor Bill Lee has halted all executions for the rest of the year while the state reviews what went wrong. The resignation is the first major leadership change since the attempted execution.
stories.headline: Tennessee prisons chief resigns after failed execution of Christa Pike

stories.body: Cornell University President Michael Kotlikoff said rape allegations connected to a fraternity house raised heartbreaking and troubling issues and pledged to review the university's handling of the matter. New York Governor Kathy Hochul has appointed Attorney General Letitia James as special prosecutor to oversee a reopened criminal investigation, saying she had lost confidence in the local district attorney's ability to manage the case.
stories.headline: Cornell faces scrutiny over handling of rape allegations at fraternity house

stories.body: Tens of thousands of people demonstrated in Madrid and other Spanish cities to demand lower rents, stronger tenant protections, an end to evictions and action against large investment landlords. The protests followed parliament's rejection of two government housing decrees that would have included measures to prevent evictions. Authorities put attendance in Madrid at about 70,000, while organizers claimed a far higher figure; most marches were peaceful, although clashes were reported in Valencia and demonstrations in Catalonia were suspended because of heavy rain.
stories.headline: Housing protests draw tens of thousands across Spain after parliament rejects emergency measures

stories.body: Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez is consulting ministers and Socialist Party leaders over whether to call an early general election after Junts joined the opposition to defeat two housing decrees. Many PSOE figures reportedly favor a 29 November election, the earliest possible date, but Sánchez has not stated his decision. The rupture has renewed doubts about the viability of his parliamentary majority, while Sumar and allied parties are assessing their strategy for a possible campaign.
stories.headline: Sánchez weighs early election after parliamentary alliance fractures over housing policy

stories.body: Spain's Senate is expected to approve a parliamentary inquiry into the mass arrival of migrants in Ceuta in late July and the government's handling of the crisis. The conservative People's Party, which holds an absolute majority in the upper chamber, says the inquiry will examine the circumstances, causes and responsibility for what it describes as an attack on national sovereignty. The vote is scheduled for Wednesday unless an early general election dissolves parliament.
stories.headline: Spain's Senate prepares inquiry into Ceuta migration crisis

stories.body: At least two people have died and another is missing after torrential rain battered Catalonia. One victim was killed when a wall collapsed at a campsite in Tordera, while a second death was reported in Montornès del Vallès; emergency services are searching for a person swept away in Pineda de Mar. Authorities have warned residents to avoid unnecessary travel, waterways and flood-prone areas as rivers rose and heavy rain shifted toward Girona province.
stories.headline: Torrential rain kills at least two people in Catalonia, with another missing

stories.body: Exceptional rainfall has caused widespread disruption across Barcelona, with more than 200 liters per square meter recorded in some parts of the city in 24 hours. The Can Bruixa station recorded more than 200 liters per square meter, its wettest day since records began, while the Observatori Fabra logged one of its wettest days since 1914. Flooding and landslides disrupted roads, metro lines and hospitals, and rail services including Rodalies and Ferrocarrils de la Generalitat were largely suspended as authorities urged people to limit travel.
stories.headline: Historic rainfall disrupts transport and daily life across Barcelona

stories.body: Catalan authorities issued emergency alerts as swollen rivers and streams created flood risks after heavy rain. The Besòs River near Santa Coloma de Gramenet reached more than 930 cubic meters per second, rising to within about 40 centimeters of its containment walls before gradually receding; residents near its mouth were advised to avoid basements and move to higher floors if necessary. Further north, Civil Protection warned people around the Daró and Ridaura rivers in the Baix Empordà to remain indoors, avoid low-lying areas and stay away from waterways.
stories.headline: Flood alerts issued as the Besòs, Daró and Ridaura rivers swell
